key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform and faster to stabilize under light, indicating reduced grain-boundary barriers and less sub-bandgap disorder.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface passivation can improve carrier landscape stability and photovoltage losses in perovskite solar cells, which is valuable for more reliable high-efficiency device design.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV) before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior surface potential contributions to localize the passivation effect
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, raised steady-state SPV from ~345 to ~417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from ~840 to ~470 s.
watch_item: These nanoscale surface-potential gains should be validated against full device performance and long-term operational stability, since KPFM probes thin-film surface dynamics rather than complete solar-cell behavior.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
